title: Span Glance: Compact Inspector Card Stack for Request Drill-down
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, scannable inspector for the Request Drill-down that surfaces span-level signals at a glance. The 'Span Glance' is a stacked card UI that consolidates the most actionable span metadata (span name, duration, error flag, correlation IDs, key tags, and top related logs) into a compact vertical rail to help engineers triage slow or failed requests without opening a full trace canvas.
acceptance_criteria: Compact inspector renders as a vertical stack of span cards next to the main timeline and remains visible while scrolling the timeline.
Each card shows span name, service, duration (p0/p50/p95), error badge, primary correlation ID, and up to 2 key tags.
Clicking a card highlights the corresponding span on the timeline and expands a lightweight flyout with quick actions (open logs, open raw span JSON, jump to full trace).
Filtering by correlation ID or tag updates the card stack in real-time and supports multi-select filters.
Keyboard navigation between cards (up/down) and activation via Enter is implemented; cards meet AA contrast and have accessible labels.
Prototype validated with 3 engineers and 1 on-call SRE in a usability session with clear preference over current dense list UX.
Design assets (Figma frame + interactive prototype) available and handed off to engineering with tokens/spacing and behavior spec.
Performance guidance provided: card stack should virtualize when >200 spans to avoid blocky render on large traces.
QA checklist enumerating visual states (normal, hovered, focused, error, long-name truncation) is included.
Implementation plan includes telemetry events for card click, flyout open, filter used for analytics and A/B evaluation.
design_notes: Rationale: current trace list is too dense for quick triage; engineers want a minimal surfacing layer that reduces cognitive overhead.
Card hierarchy emphasizes duration and error first, then correlation ID so ops can immediately correlate cross-service requests.
We use micro-animations (fade/highlight) to connect cards to timeline spans to preserve spatial mapping while reducing context switching.
Stack should collapse into a single compact pill on small width breakpoints (<720px) with a slide-over inspector to conserve vertical space.
Tag selection supports typeahead and pinned tags; design recommends showing top 3 tags derived from runtime sampling to avoid noise.
Accessibility: each card exposes aria-describedby linking to span summary; color alone not used to indicate errors (icons + text present).
Trade-offs: full span detail is intentionally omitted from cards to keep them lightweight; heavy details open in flyout/trace view.
Virtualization: engineering must implement windowing for large traces; prototype uses placeholder shimmer for offscreen cards.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sketch session with PM (Ravi Kumar) and Eng lead (Maya Lopez). Agreed on card fields and interaction model.
2026-03-05: Mid-fidelity frames completed in Figma; shared with SRE rotation for early feedback. Updated visual density after session.
2026-03-08: Interactive prototype built (principle animations + keyboard nav). Demoed to eng and PM; eng requested telemetry hooks and virtualization notes.
2026-03-10: Usability test with 3 engineers + 1 on-call SRE. Observed 45% faster time-to-identify-failure vs baseline list. Logged issues for long service names and mobile collapse.
2026-03-12: Incorporating review feedback; preparing final handoff docs and QA checklist. This ticket moved to In Review for design signoff.
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Kumar): love the compactness, request adding a cost-estimate micro-indicator (approx token cost per request) for high-latency spans tied to Optimize insights.
Eng (Maya Lopez): implementation ok but require strict virtualization for traces >200 spans; requested transition perf metrics and a fallback to paginated list for extreme cases.
SRE (Noah Singh): suggested making correlation ID copy-to-clipboard one-click and adding link to related logs filtered by span id.
Design (peer review - Lina Gomez): recommended tighter truncation rules and suggested a subtle color band to denote service ownership for faster visual scanning.
Accessibility reviewer (Samira Khan): confirmed keyboard flows but requested explicit focus styles for high-contrast mode.
next_steps: Finalize Figma frames with remaining tweaks (cost micro-indicator, copy icon) by 2026-03-14.
Create engineering handoff doc with behavior matrix, telemetry event spec, and virtualization guidance by 2026-03-16.
Design pair with eng for first sprint planning; propose 2-sprint build: sprint 1 (cards + flyout + filters), sprint 2 (keyboard nav, virtualization, mobile collapse).
Schedule A/B experiment with PM to measure triage time and click-to-log for 4 weeks post-launch.
Follow-up ticket to add Optimize cost signals integration (PM-1205) after initial launch.
